$comment: The quality benchmark's metric dictionary (FR-043-AC-1..AC-6, CR-098; agent-ix/quoin#198). NORMATIVE: a metric that does not declare unit, population and method is not one this benchmark emits, and `loadMetrics` refuses the file rather than reporting a gap. This is the same rule agent-ix/quire-rs FR-063 applies to the engine's own numbers, applied one layer up to the thing that scores the engine. Distinct from quire-rs's `bench/manifest.json`, which scores ENGINE coverage figures; this scores the toolchain's FINDING quality.

finding_precision.population: findings the toolchain reported for one labelled defect family
finding_precision.method: truePositives / (truePositives + falsePositives) per family, from evals/lib/quality.mjs scoreFindings. A finding is paired to a label by LOCATION where both name one, so a right-family wrong-place finding is a false positive (CR-098); a family with no denominator reports null, never 0, because 0/0 is not 0% and a precision of 0 claims the run was wrong
finding_precision.baseline_note: Per-family, so the numbers live in `bench/tier1-baseline.json` rather than here — one scalar cannot hold eight families, and averaging them is the exact hiding this metric exists to prevent. First scored run (2026-08-23, quire built from quire-rs@8c4928a): five families at 1.00, three with no denominator because nothing fired on them. `null` here still means no single figure is declared, NOT zero.

finding_recall.population: labelled defects in one family that the corpus declares findable; a label marked findable:false is excluded from the denominator AND reported
finding_recall.method: truePositives / (truePositives + misses) per family, from scoreFindings. Reported PER FAMILY and never averaged: a tool that finds every marker mismatch and no vacuous suite has a respectable average and a hole, and the average is what hides it
finding_recall.baseline_note: Per-family, in `bench/tier1-baseline.json`. First scored run (2026-08-23): catch-all-universal, hollow-denominator, marker-form-mismatch, undeclared-type-value and vacuous-under-guard at 1.00; gate-that-gates-nothing, mocked-confirmation and oracle-is-code-copy at 0.00 for three DIFFERENT reasons — no detector, a detector with no producer (quoin#204), and a detector with no caller (quire-rs#236). The tier-2 key records 7 findings, 0 of which the tools found at battletest pass 2; that 0-of-7 is the recall this programme exists to move.

finding_precision.unadjudicated.population: findings of one ADVISORY family, on corpus cases whose `expect.yaml` names that family's reason in neither `diagnostic_reasons` nor `absent_diagnostic_reasons`
finding_precision.unadjudicated.method: counted per family by evals/lib/quality.mjs scopedPrecision, from the rulings bench-tier1.mjs adjudicationOf reads out of each case's own expect.yaml. THE NUMBER AN ADVISORY ACTUALLY REPORTS. Its precision RATE cannot fall independently of agent-ix/qa-corpus's own `make ci` — a firing on a case that declared the reason absent turns that gate red first — so a rate of 1.00 is not evidence the detector is right. This is: it is the number of times the toolchain fired and nobody has ruled on whether it should have. Ratcheted lower-is-better, so an advisory that starts firing more widely costs something and the corpus adjudication work has a number to move
finding_precision.unadjudicated.baseline_note: Per-family, so the counts live in `bench/tier1-baseline.json` under each advisory family's `precision_basis`. Introduced by agent-ix/quoin#245 after the run that opened it measured 313 unadjudicated of 316 firings for `archetype-matches-nothing` and 64 of 66 for `catch-all-universal` — 377 findings on which the benchmark held no opinion and said nothing. `null` here means no single figure is declared, NOT zero.

span_grounding_rate.population: acceptance criteria the FR-052 classifier gives a specific property shape
span_grounding_rate.method: criteria whose domain, precondition AND oracle spans are all present, over criteria carrying a specific shape. NOT YET COMPUTED: no runner reads `quire properties --json` for this, tracked as agent-ix/quoin#219. Declared here because the dictionary is the contract and a metric nobody declared is a metric nobody can ask for
span_grounding_rate.baseline_note: Battletest pass 2 measured 0 of 65 specific-shape records carrying all three spans. Zero is the measured starting point, not an absence.

actionability_rate.population: findings the toolchain emitted across the corpus entry
actionability_rate.method: findings naming a row id or a document line, over findings emitted, from scoreActionability. A finding you cannot act on is a finding nobody acts on, whatever its precision
actionability_rate.baseline_note: Battletest pass 2 measured 15 of 496 findings carrying a row id — 3.02%. Tier 1's first scored run reads 2 of 7 (29%): a small, clean corpus flatters the figure, which is why the tier-2 number is the one to move and both are kept.

cost_per_confirmed_insight.unit: tokens and tool calls per true positive
cost_per_confirmed_insight.population: findings CONFIRMED as true positives, not findings emitted
cost_per_confirmed_insight.method: tokenUsage.total / truePositives and toolCalls / truePositives, from scoreCost, extending the FR-042 eval report metrics rather than opening a second accounting. Both numbers, because they are different costs: tokens are the context budget and tool calls are wall-clock and blast radius. Reports null per-insight when nothing was confirmed — dividing by emitted output would reward a run for producing more of it
cost_per_confirmed_insight.baseline_note: COMPUTED SINCE agent-ix/quoin#243. `scoreCost` was complete in `evals/lib/quality.mjs` and reached by nothing but its own unit tests; `scripts/bench-tier1.mjs` imported only `scoreActionability` and `scoreFindings`. For a TIER-1 run `tokens` is `null` and not 0: this runner shells out to `quire` and `quoin` and calls no model, so the token cost is not measured here rather than measured at zero — the tokens half belongs to the FR-042 eval harness, which is an agent run. The tool-call half IS this benchmark's cost and is counted exactly. Per-family baselines are not meaningful for a cost; the figure lives in `bench/tier1-baseline.json` beside the run that spent it.

sentinel.silent_zero.population: metrics emitted across every corpus entry in the run
sentinel.silent_zero.method: ratio-shaped metrics with matched = 0 over a non-zero population and NO accompanying diagnostic. A count-shaped metric is exempt (CR-098): matched and its value are the same fact, so a zero reports that none was found, not that none was read. This is the shape of `555/2389 (23%)` published over a corpus the binder could not read
sentinel.silent_zero.baseline_note: A GATE, not a score. Expected exactly 0 with no tolerance, and it never ratchets: a benchmark that let this score 0.98 and pass would be measuring the wrong thing. COMPUTED SINCE agent-ix/quoin#243 — declared here from the beginning and evaluated by no code until then, so a reader of this file saw seven governed metrics and four producers. The condition is `matched == 0` over a NON-ZERO `examined`, which is the engine's own wording in `coverage.backed`'s `method`; `examined == 0` is a population the instrument had nothing to walk, not one it failed to read, and is reported under `unread_population` rather than gated. Gating on the looser reading fired on three fixtures — `catch-all-properties`, `greenfield-no-symbols`, `gate-that-gates-nothing` — every one of which seeds a symbol-less tree on purpose. First measured run: 0 violations, 3 unread populations (agent-ix/quire-rs#271).

minting.section_hit_rate.unit: fraction of (trace target, minting document) pairs
minting.section_hit_rate.population: the pairs `quire coverage` reports over the SCORED cases of the tier-1 corpus — a trace target's `archetype:` selects a document and its `exclude:` keeps it. Pending cases are excluded, the same population every other tier-1 number is drawn from
minting.section_hit_rate.method: `matched` summed over `examined` summed, across every scored case whose `quire coverage --json` payload carries the metric in state `measured`. `null` — never 0 — when NO case reports it, which is exactly what an engine predating agent-ix/quire-rs#270 looks like: absent and zero are different claims. REPORTED, NOT RATCHETED: the value is a property of the corpus POPULATION, since a seeded section mismatch lowers it and its control raises it, so ratcheting it would score fixture authorship rather than the toolchain. What it is here for is the ENGINE axis — the metric's presence is the signal that #270 landed
minting.section_hit_rate.baseline_note: No baseline, deliberately: see `method`. Measured 2026-08-24 over the expanded corpus — `null` at engine `84740d4` (no case reports the metric; it does not exist) and measured at engine `816e187`. This metric appearing on every case was ONE of the two Wave 3 payload signals the tier-1 runner did not read, and the reason `bench/wave3-before-after.md` scored every family `held` (agent-ix/quoin#236).

finding_localisation_rate.population: true positives from a scored tier-1 run
finding_localisation_rate.method: positional pairings over true positives, from evals/lib/quality.mjs scoreFindings. A finding pairs positionally only when it and its label BOTH name a place and the places agree, so this is the share of confirmed findings that said where. It is the metric that encodes the actual requirement — an alert nobody can locate is an alert nobody acts on — and it is deliberately not per-family: the question is about the toolchain's output, not about one detector
finding_localisation_rate.baseline_note: 0.40 on the first scored tier-1 run (2026-08-23): 2 of 5 true positives named where. 0.60 after quire-rs#256 gave `no-symbol-bound` an unbound symbol to name instead of a language. 0.80 after quire-rs#261 made `catch-all-universal` a located diagnostic instead of a moving aggregate. The one remaining miss is `hollow-denominator`, whose diagnostic names a METRIC and carries no path — arguably correct, since a hollow ratio is a fact about a corpus rather than about a file, and the label records that.
